title: aia_extract drops non-HTTP URI schemes inside pkix-chain instead of deferring to AiaFetcher
close_reason:
Half fixed -- the diagnosability half, which is what the bead actually complained about. The design question it raises is recorded in the code and left for you.

What the bead gets exactly right: "The contributor only debugging signal is fetcher was constructed, never called, chain validation fails with PathBuild(NoPathFound). There is no error variant pointing at we filtered out URIs we deemed unfetchable. AiaError::UriUnsupported, which is the right signal, never fires because pkix-chain made the decision for the fetcher."

All true, and UriUnsupported(String) already existed in the enum. It now fires: when the extractor declines a caIssuers URI for its scheme, the URI is kept and, if nothing else failed, the build returns Error::Aia(AiaError::UriUnsupported(uri)). The error names the URI and attributes the decision to this crate rather than the fetcher.

Precedence is deliberate: a fetch that was attempted and failed is more informative than one never tried, so the report only applies when last_aia_error is None. Tested both ways (a_real_fetch_failure_outranks_the_excluded_uri_report pins a 503 surviving).

Implementation note: ca_issuers_http_uris and ca_issuers_unsupported_uris are two views of ONE walk, parameterised by which side of the scheme test to yield, so they cannot drift -- a URI is reported excluded exactly when it was not offered.

What I did NOT do, and why: the bead larger point is that the AiaFetcher trait says "caller decides what is fetchable" while pkix-chain hardcodes http-only, and that this is the design lock-in zkjb.4 created the trait to avoid. That critique stands. But removing the filter is not free: it is also what stops a file:// caIssuers URI from reaching a fetcher that might honour it, and net-guard only covers resolved IPs for HTTP, not file://. The clean shape is to let the fetcher declare its schemes (a supports_scheme method defaulting to http-only), which is an additive change to a published trait AND a defaulted trait method -- the exact hazard recorded in the forwarding-impls memory, since the &T and Arc<T> forwarding impls would have to forward it or silently answer wrong. That is an API decision for you; the tradeoff is now written into ca_issuers_unsupported_uris rustdoc so it is not rediscovered from scratch.

Fixture: leaf-via-intermediate-ldap-aia.der, caIssuers URI ldap://ldap.example.test/cn=intermediate,dc=example,dc=test. Verified by mutation -- removing the report makes the test fail with PathBuild(NoPathFound), the symptom itself. The test fetcher panics if called, so exclusion-before-fetch is pinned too.

Second full fixture regeneration this session, for the same reason as q9hv.16: gen.py calls ec.generate_private_key per run. Seeding that root deterministically would make future fixture additions a one-file diff; worth doing if more are coming.

Gates green: fmt, clippy, rustdoc, typos, 2348 tests.
